fun_highlights: The callback card system is genuinely satisfying: 'looked away' at age 10 comes back at 49 as a stranger sleeping rough, and at 57 as a chance to redeem it — the reach-back across forty years feels earned and particular in a way that no other browser sim delivers.

Vocation x era intersections (vx_soldier_war, vx_scholar_turning, vx_maker_plenty) produce genuinely distinct life-shapes: a soldier born into war reads nothing like a maker born in fat years, and the coloring is mechanical, not just cosmetic.

Dynasty-level accumulation creates real 'one more generation' pull in mid-run: watching a house climb from 'rented room' to 'old and famous house' across five lives (Quint, Thorne) with a crystallized motto and a specific reputation is the strongest motivation spike in the game.

The collateral succession mechanic and the ~20-25% childless/solitary life rate meaningfully break the domestic-arc monoculture visible in older versions; solitary elder cards (e_solitary, e_childless) give those lives a proper resolution rather than a dead end.

Prose line rotation (freshPick + RECENT_LINES dedup) genuinely keeps the ambient log from repeating verbatim across dozens of lives; the observation pool is deep enough that the ambient voice stays fresh well past dynasty 8.
Fate cards (f_fire, f_sudden_loss, f_grace, f_reversal) that simply happen — no choosing your way out — create memorable ruptures and break the player's sense that they control everything.
staleness: Beat order within a life is functionally invariant by dynasty 4-5: c_origin (age 3-5) → 1-2 child cards → y_calling (age 14-22) → y_love1 or a_meet_late → a_marry → a_child → a_work or midlife cards → elder cards → death. The calling card and the love card are near-certain due to their boosted draw-weights. Across 40+ lives in the transcript, every single life that survived youth followed this five-beat spine. The genre licenses a gentle tempo, but sameness of arc shape (not just content) is the central staleness problem.

The calling card (y_calling) fires in literally every life, always in youth (14-22), always presenting the same four roads. The framing varies by era/seat, but the choice and its age-band are a fixed structural pillar every player encounters every life. By dynasty 6, the player already knows 'here comes the calling card' before the text resolves.

The love and marriage pipeline is heavily forced: even with 30% nudge on y_love1 and 5% on a_meet_late, the engine almost always routes a love card by adult stage (only 2 of 40+ lives in the transcript were genuinely solitary all the way through). The mechanical pressure means this is less a discovery than a scheduled event.

Callback cards, while individually good, repeat across dynasties: cb_lookaway fires in Dynasties 1, 2, 10, 12, 13, 14 — six times across fifteen dynasties. cb_corner fires four times. Because the memories that gate them (looked_away, cut_a_corner) are among the most-drawn choices, the 'long arc closing' payoff stops feeling like a payoff by dynasty 8 and starts feeling like a known sequence.

The elder band is structurally thin for non-domestic lives. Solitary/childless elders do get their own cards (e_solitary, e_childless, e_solitary), but vocation-specific elder caps (e_soldier_old, e_scholar_old, e_wanderer_old, e_maker_handoff) are once-per-dynasty and once the dynasty has burned them, all subsequent elders — of that calling — fall through to the generic pool (e_legacy, e_garden, e_peace, e_body, e_last_walk). By dynasty 5+ this makes elder years feel interchangeable regardless of calling.

Reputation monoculture persists at scale: across 15 dynasties, 9 mottos appear in the transcript. 'What we have, we share' appears TWICE (dynasties 3 and 9), and the dominant mottos are 'scholarly' and 'kind' variants. The reputation math, despite balancing efforts, still collapses many houses toward teaching/generosity arcs because those choices appear in the largest number of common cards.

The era system underdelivers. Of 15 dynasties, 6 are 'war', 2 'plague', 1 'hard', 1 'plenty', 1 'turning', and 4 'settled'. The war era in particular fires its two dedicated cards (w_war_call, w_war_loss) almost identically: 'go when called / find a way out' + 'let the grief in / bury it in work'. By the 4th war dynasty, these read as scheduled callbacks rather than surprising history.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 alternative structural spines so the beat ORDER itself varies: a 'late bloomer' life that skips calling and love until adult, a 'short fierce life' template that compresses to 5-7 cards before early death, a 'contemplative' life that draws more universal/entropy cards and fewer milestone cards. Gate these structurally — not via content gating — so the player cannot predict 'here comes the calling card' on every run.
improvements.why: The single invariant spine (origin → calling → love → marry → child → work → midlife → elder) is the deepest staleness problem. Content variety cannot overcome it because the player learns the skeleton by dynasty 3. A differently-paced life feels like a different game, not just different text.

improvements.what: Cap callback card frequency by gating on dynasty-count: cb_lookaway, cb_corner, and cb_books_late should each fire at most once across an entire session (using the global RECENT_LINES or a S.seenSession set), not just once per life. When the gate is burned, substitute a different thematically-adjacent callback instead of re-triggering the same arc.
improvements.why: The 'long arc closing' feel of callbacks — their primary emotional value — depends on rarity. cb_lookaway firing six times in fifteen dynasties makes it a scheduled event, not a surprise. The onceDyn flag stops it repeating in the same house but not across different houses in the same session.

improvements.what: Add a second tier of era-specific cards for war and plague (the two most common eras): e.g., a war era 'years after' card (for adults who were children during the war), a plague era 'immunity survivor' card, a 'remembrance' card for a generation born after the war. Currently each era has only 2-4 dedicated cards that are once-per-life/dynasty; by dynasty 4 the era feels like a one-time flavour coat rather than a living historical backdrop.
improvements.why: Era variety is the game's most structurally elegant lever — being born into 'war' vs. 'turning' should produce a meaningfully different set of possible moments, not just different framing on the calling card and two event cards. Deeper era card pools would make the macro-history layer do more work.

improvements.what: Introduce 2-3 'anti-domestic' life-shapes that reliably produce no calling/love/child arc — lives anchored instead around craft mastery, political identity, or intellectual obsession. These would use a different set of milestone cards entirely (an alternative to y_calling that gates a completely separate adult arc without love/family as scaffold). Currently ~20-25% of lives are childless but almost all still have love and calling; true structural alternatives remain rare.
improvements.why: The 'variety of lives' criterion in this genre means structural variety, not just content variety. A scholar who married late and a scholar who never married but built a school are not structurally different under the current system — they draw from the same card pool with one branch missing.

improvements.what: Deepen the elder band for players past dynasty 5 by adding once-per-session (not once-per-dynasty) elder cards: an 'old and famous' card available only to lives in seat-5+ houses, a 'dynasty historian' card where the elder reads the whole lineage and comments on it, a 'founding myth distortion' card where a great-grandchild's version of an ancestor's deed has drifted into legend. These would fire only once per session, providing a genuine 'I haven't seen this before' moment in the late game.
improvements.why: The elder band is the session's closing act on every life, and it does the most work in long sessions. After dynasty 5, players have seen every elder card; the elder years become a wait for death rather than a final act with its own interest.

verdict: The writing and the dynasty-accumulation arc are genuinely good, and the callback system delivers real pleasure through dynasty 4 — but by dynasty 6-8 the invariant five-beat life-spine (origin, calling, love, child, elder), the repeat-firing of the same callbacks, and the shallow era card pools converge into a recognizable template that patient content variety cannot fully disguise, putting a firm ceiling on long-session freshness.
